findings.title: Backup code login skips both the password check and TOTP
findings.description: The password is only verified when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy (line 121), and the new branch at line 131 takes precedence over TOTP whenever `credentials.backupCode` is truthy. A request with `email`, any non-empty `totpCode` (never validated in this branch) and one valid `backupCode` therefore authenticates with no password and no TOTP. The identity-provider guard at line 113 is skipped the same way. The codes are offered as a plaintext download and clipboard copy, so one leaked code becomes a complete single-factor credential. The `!credentials.totpCode` skip is pre-existing, but this change extends it to a new credential type. The backup branch should require a verified password (e.g. reject `backupCode` combined with `totpCode`).

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.description: The code decrypts the list, checks `indexOf`, nulls the entry and writes the whole blob back with an unconditional `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the check, so "used exactly once" (the `backup_code_instructions` text) is not guaranteed. Concurrent use of two different codes can also resurrect one of them through a lost update. Use a conditional update on the previously read ciphertext, or a transaction.

findings.title: Unvalidated `backupCode` input and unguarded decrypt/parse
findings.description: `req.body.backupCode` comes from a JSON body and is used as `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` with no type check. A truthy non-string value (`123`, `["a"]`, `{}`) throws a `TypeError` and yields an unhandled 500. `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is also unguarded and untyped (`any`) here and in `next-auth-options.ts:139-141`, so a corrupt value or rotated key throws a raw error, and a non-array result is not caught. Validate the body with zod, as elsewhere in the repo, and parse the decrypted value into `(string | null)[]`.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves the UI stale
findings.description: After `enable` succeeds, 2FA is on server-side, but `onEnable()` is now deferred to the Close button (lines 266-270). The parent's `onOpenChange` (`apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64`) only toggles `open`. Dismissing with Escape or an overlay click therefore never runs `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` or `resetState()`. The modal also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening it shows the old codes instead of the password step. Call `onEnable()` when enable succeeds, or route dismissal through the same close handler.

findings.title: Backup codes and secrets persist in client state; blob URL is never revoked on close
findings.description: `resetState` clears only `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`. `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `secret`, `dataUri` and the form's `totpCode` survive closing the modal. The object URL holding the plaintext codes is only revoked when setup runs again (line 98), never on close or unmount.

findings.title: `type="password"` prop disables the visibility toggle in the enable modal
findings.description: The field was changed from `TextField` to `PasswordField` but still passes `type="password"`. `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:36-39`), so the caller's `type` always wins. The eye button toggles its icon but the input never becomes visible. Remove the `type` prop.

findings.title: Backup-code form constraints are ineffective on login; matching is case-sensitive
findings.description:
- **Empty submit on login:** the login form is `noValidate` (`apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:188`) and the zod schema passes `backupCode` through, so `required`/`minLength` do nothing. An empty code falls into the TOTP branch, returns `SecondFactorRequired`, and `login.tsx:156` only calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)`. The user gets no error.
- **Case sensitivity:** codes are lowercase hex (`setup.ts:61`) but the placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, and the server only strips dashes (`next-auth-options.ts:144`, `disable.ts:61`). Uppercase or whitespace-padded input fails as "incorrect". Normalise with `.trim().toLowerCase()`.
- **Exhausted codes:** once all codes are nulled, the error is `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than `MissingBackupCodes`.

findings.title: Backup-code verification duplicated across two endpoints
findings.description: The key check, decrypt, `JSON.parse`, dash-strip and `indexOf` sequence is copy-pasted from `next-auth-options.ts:131-145`. The log message at `disable.ts:50` still says "cannot proceed with backup code login" in the disable endpoint. Extract a shared helper (e.g. `verifyBackupCode(encrypted, input)`) so normalisation and future hardening live in one place.

findings.title: `BackupCode.tsx` exports a component named `TwoFactor`
findings.description: The default export is `function TwoFactor(...)`, copied from `TwoFactor.tsx`. React DevTools and stack traces will show two different `TwoFactor` components. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

findings.title: Loose typing of backup-code state
findings.description: `useState([])` infers `never[]`. It only compiles because `body` is `any` and `never` is assignable to `string` in `formatBackupCode(code)`. Use `useState<string[]>([])` and type the setup response.

findings.title: Critical backup-code paths are untested; known-broken assertion left with a FIXME
findings.description:
- **Missing coverage:** the only new coverage is the download filename and a toast. Login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, incorrect/missing-code errors and disabling 2FA with a backup code are deferred via the TODO at line 12, and there are no unit tests for the `authorize` branch.
- **Vacuous copy check:** the toast at `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278-279` fires whether or not `clipboard.writeText` succeeds, so lines 120-121 assert nothing about the copy.
- **Vacuous switch check:** the diff adds a FIXME (lines 50-51) instead of fixing line 53. `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise and always passes; the fix is `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order globally
findings.description: `tabIndex={-1}` on the show/hide button in the shared `PasswordField` makes it unreachable by keyboard everywhere the component is used (login, signup, settings). This is an accessibility regression in a shared UI primitive, made as a side effect of an unrelated feature.

findings.title: Clipboard write is not awaited or error-handled
findings.description: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught. The success toast shows even when the write is rejected (permission denied, insecure context).

findings.title: Smaller structural points in the enable modal
findings.description:
- `DisplayBackupCodes` is inserted second in `SetupStep` although it is the last step, which silently renumbers the enum.
- `formatBackupCode` (line 163) is a pure helper declared inside the component, after the handler that uses it.
- The download control nests a `<button>` inside an `<a>` (lines 283-287), which is invalid interactive nesting.
- The `user` Omit list in `packages/trpc/server/createContext.ts:18-27` excludes `twoFactorSecret` but not the new `backupCodes`.

findings.title: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted rather than hashed
findings.description: This matches how `twoFactorSecret` is stored, and 5 bytes from `crypto.randomBytes` is adequate entropy. But the codes are only ever compared, so per-code hashes would avoid recoverable plaintext if `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` leaks. The `indexOf` comparison is also not constant-time, which matters little given the rate limiting at `next-auth-options.ts:109`.

findings.title: Schema, migration, fixtures and i18n are consistent
findings.description:
- The nullable `backupCodes String?` column and the migration are additive and safe.
- `buildUser` in `packages/lib/test/builder.ts:192` is updated.
- All new translation keys exist in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:2013-2019`.
- `disable.ts:107` clears `backupCodes` together with the secret.
- `getUserFromSession` uses an explicit `select` (`packages/trpc/server/middlewares/sessionMiddleware.ts:24-76`), so the encrypted codes are not exposed through the tRPC user context.

findings.title: Error-code handling in the disable modal fixed to an exclusive chain
findings.description: The former independent `if` blocks let the final `else` overwrite the `IncorrectPassword` and `SecondFactorRequired` messages with "something went wrong". The `else if` chain fixes that and adds the two new codes.
